anti_patterns.name: Raw SQL string interpolation
anti_patterns.description: Login and search build SQL by concatenating request text instead of using bound parameters, so each route must be fixed individually and the pattern recurs.

anti_patterns.name: Missing server-side authorization layer
anti_patterns.description: Ownership and role checks are implemented route by route, with no central enforcement, so many routes omit them and a single fix will not close the gap.

anti_patterns.name: SPA without BFF
anti_patterns.description: The Angular frontend keeps the session token in script-readable storage and no backend-for-frontend holds it server-side, so any script injection yields a reusable token.

anti_patterns.name: Secrets hardcoded in source
anti_patterns.description: Signing keys and other secrets are committed to the repository rather than a managed store, so repository access alone enables forged logins.
